definitions.explanation: An updated or revised version of a published work such as a book, textbook, dictionary, or manual, incorporating corrections or new content compared to earlier printings.

examples.japanese: この{辞書|じしょ}の{新版|しんぱん}が{来月|らいげつ}{発売|はつばい}される。
examples.english: The new edition of this dictionary will go on sale next month.

examples.japanese: {旧版|きゅうばん}と{新版|しんぱん}の{違|ちが}いは、{巻末|かんまつ}の{索引|さくいん}が{充実|じゅうじつ}した{点|てん}だ。
examples.english: The difference between the old and new editions is that the index at the end has been expanded.

notes:
A compound of {新|しん} (new) and {版|ぱん} (edition/version). Used for updated or revised versions of books, textbooks, software, and other published works. The reading is しんぱん (with rendaku on {版|はん}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新版|しんぱん}を{出|だ}す: to release a new edition
- {新版|しんぱん}が{出|で}る: a new edition comes out
- {改訂|かいてい}{新版|しんぱん}: revised new edition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {改訂版|かいていばん} — revised edition (emphasizes revision of content)
- {増補版|ぞうほばん} — expanded edition (content added)
- {旧版|きゅうばん} — old edition (the opposite)
- {初版|しょはん} — first edition
